paper_title: Shifting Long-Context LLMs Research from Input to Output
caption: Proportion of real-user demand: The aforementioned 2K range refers to the interval [2K, 4K), and similarly for the other ranges. Solid color fill for input demand, slash fill for output demand in the Wildchat dataset.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the distribution of real-user demand across different context length ranges (2K, 4K, 8K, and 16K) in the Wildchat dataset, distinguishing between input and output demands using visual encoding: solid-colored bars represent input demand, while diagonally slashed bars represent output demand. The vertical axis, labeled “Number,” ranges from 0 to 120,000 in increments of 20,000, indicating the absolute count of instances. For the 2K range (defined as [2K, 4K)), input demand is 9,320 (solid yellow bar) and output demand is 78,188 (yellow with diagonal slashes). In the 4K range ([4K, 8K)), input demand is 3,784 (solid orange bar) and output demand is 108,494 (orange with diagonal slashes). For the 8K range ([8K, 16K)), input demand is 1,401 (solid cyan bar) and output demand is 17,865 (cyan with diagonal slashes). In the 16K range ([16K, ∞)), input demand is 832 (solid dark blue bar) and output demand is 4,247 (dark blue with diagonal slashes). The chart visually emphasizes that output demand vastly exceeds input demand across all ranges, with the 4K-output category being the highest at 108,494, followed by 2K-output at 78,188, while 16K-input is the lowest at 832. The legend at the bottom clearly maps each color and fill pattern to its corresponding category, enabling direct comparison between input and output demands within each context length bin.
